hero.title: We make the antiques and art market easier to understand.
hero.subtitle: Aura Historia exists for collectors and professionals who value careful discovery, reliable context, and a calm view of a scattered international market.

mission.title: Orientation without flattening the field.
mission.p1: Antiques and art often surface far from the obvious channels: with specialist dealers, smaller shops, auction houses, and marketplaces shaped by local vocabulary and cataloguing habits.
mission.p2: We build Aura Historia to bring order to that search without turning it into a generic shopping experience. The aim is simple: help knowledgeable people see more, compare with care, and keep the original seller relationship clear.

values.title: Restraint before noise.
values.description: These principles shape our product decisions, our language, and the way we present sources.

carefulClaims.title: Careful claims
carefulClaims.description: We avoid inflated promises about value, authenticity, or certainty. Aura Historia supports discovery and research; judgement remains with the collector and the source.

discernment.title: Respect for expertise
discernment.description: Our users are discerning. The product, interface, and copy should inform clearly without patronising, sensationalising, or rushing the decision.

sourceStewardship.title: Source stewardship
sourceStewardship.description: We keep context, attribution, and the original seller relationship visible so research does not become an anonymous list of objects.

team.title: A small team with a long view.
team.description: The people behind Aura Historia combine product work, research discipline, and market intelligence.

julianBruder.bio: Julian has collected antique art for years, with a particular interest in oil paintings of the Virgin Mary. He may publish parts of his collection soon and uses Aura Historia in his own collecting work.

lucaFranke.bio: Luca leads the web application work, translating Aura Historia's research and discovery goals into a reliable, maintainable product experience.

abdellahFilali.bio: Abdellah works on the automation behind source ingestion, data quality, and repeatable processes that help the platform follow a fragmented market at scale.

erwinBause.bio: Erwin shapes the interface and interaction details so Aura Historia remains calm, legible, and respectful of how collectors and specialists actually research objects.

antonDiettrich.bio: Anton works on the knowledge graph foundations that connect objects, sources, categories, and market context with more structure and continuity.

discover.title: The antiques market is global. Discovery is still fragmented.
discover.p1: Antiques have moved online, but inventory remains split across dealer websites, auction calendars, marketplaces, and local shops. Aura Historia brings that scattered supply into one calm, curated platform view.
discover.p2: For collectors, decorators, and the trade, that means fewer blind spots: more sources, more context, and a better chance of finding the object others have not noticed yet.

artworkStories.title: The global antiques market in one view
artworkStories.description: The right objects rarely sit in a single auction feed. They surface with small dealers, specialist shops, marketplaces, and auctions — often under local terms and only for a short window. Aura Historia turns this scattered market into something you can see, read, and act on.

connoisseurship.title: See beyond the listing
connoisseurship.description: Holbein’s The Ambassadors is a painting about knowledge, instruments, and hidden perspective. In antiques, too, the decisive clue is often not only in the listing, but in the images, source, provenance, price movement or timing.
connoisseurship.supporting: Aura Historia gathers these signals in a calm working view: search, compare, save, and act in time — without losing the pleasure of discovery.

globalCollecting.title: The cabinet of wonders is distributed now
globalCollecting.description: The Paston Treasure shows luxury objects, naturalia, and rarities from a worldwide trade network. Today’s collecting cabinet is no longer in one room; it is spread across dealer sites, marketplaces, auction calendars, and local specialists.
globalCollecting.supporting: Aura Historia does not replace those sources. The platform leads you to them — after it has continuously indexed the scattered supply, made it legible, and monitored it for what you are looking for.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: A precise overview of how Aura Historia makes the global antiques market easier to follow.

howItWorks.question: What is Aura Historia?
howItWorks.answer: Aura Historia is a global platform for antiques, art, and distinctive objects. We bring current inventory from dealer sites, auction houses, marketplaces, and specialist sources into one place so collectors and professionals can follow the market with clarity.

directPurchase.question: Can I buy directly through Aura Historia?
directPurchase.answer: Purchases take place with the original seller. Aura Historia takes you to the source listing so you can verify price, availability, shipping, condition, and payment terms directly before you buy or bid.

priceAlerts.question: What can I monitor?
priceAlerts.answer: Your private watchlist keeps found objects in view and can notify you about relevant changes such as price movements or status updates. Search alerts monitor the market for new matches that fit your criteria.

language.question: Does Aura Historia work across languages?
language.answer: Yes. Aura Historia is built for international discovery: listings may appear in different languages, categories, and dealer vocabularies. The platform helps bridge that fragmentation without requiring you to know every local term.

updateFrequency.question: How current are the listings?
updateFrequency.answer: We refresh sources continuously. Final availability, however, always belongs to the dealer, auction house, or marketplace, so critical details should be checked on the original listing before purchase or bid.

dealers.question: Which sources are included?
dealers.answer: We include trusted dealers, specialist shops, auction houses, and marketplaces — including smaller sources that are often less visible on auction-focused platforms. Coverage is expanded continuously.

dealerRequest.question: Can I suggest a dealer or source?
dealerRequest.answer: Yes. Send the URL and a short note to contact@aura-historia.com. We review whether the source is relevant, reputable, and technically suitable for inclusion.

comparisonBarnebys.question: How is Aura Historia different from auction aggregators?
comparisonBarnebys.answer: Auction aggregators are strongest around upcoming or past auction lots. Aura Historia looks at the market more broadly: dealer inventory, specialist shops, marketplaces, and auctions in one platform — with watchlists, search alerts, and market monitoring.

comparisonPriceDatabase.question: Is Aura Historia a price database?
comparisonPriceDatabase.answer: No. Historical auction prices can be useful, but they do not automatically show what is available now. Aura Historia focuses on current discovery, monitoring, and timely market signals.

free.question: What does the partner program cost?
free.answer: The partner program is entirely free. There are no setup, listing or sales fees – we don't earn from your sales.

cancel.question: Can I leave at any time?
cancel.answer: Yes. You can end your partnership at any time, without notice and without giving a reason. We remove your products on request right away.

technical.question: Do I need technical skills?
technical.answer: No. For WooCommerce and Shopify, a single click installs everything. Our extension handles the rest. Only the custom API integration benefits from development experience.

exclusivity.question: Do I have to sell exclusively through Aura Historia?
exclusivity.answer: No. You keep selling on your own website and every other platform you already use. We bring you additional traffic – we don't replace anything.

data.question: What happens to my product data?
data.answer: We only sync publicly visible product information to make it discoverable in our search. Purchases happen on your website. You retain full control over your data.

transactions.question: Are sales processed through Aura Historia?
transactions.answer: No. Buyers are sent straight to your shop to complete the purchase. You keep your customer relationship, your payment processing and 100% of your revenue.

fit.question: Which shops fit the program?
fit.answer: We look for reputable online shops selling antiques, art, collectibles and comparable historical objects. Auction houses and specialised dealers are explicitly welcome.

support.question: Will I get help during setup?
support.answer: Yes. Our partner team supports you personally during onboarding and is reachable by email – also long after launch.

hero.title: Connect your shop with our API
hero.subtitle: Connect your inventory through a provider you have access to. Synchronous batches return completed write results; inspect failures before retrying.

concept.title: Synchronous listing batches
concept.description: POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE complete writes synchronously. HTTP 200 contains only failed entries; [] means every entry succeeded, including an empty batch. Search visibility is a separate step.

synchronous.title: Completed results
synchronous.description: Each entry has its own transaction. Successful writes remain committed when another entry fails.

retry.title: Retry precisely
retry.description: For a partial failure, correct and retry only failed entries where appropriate. If all entries fail, inspect the problem response.

summary.title: What you need for the first sync
summary.subtitle: These three pieces are enough to send a first, easy-to-check product batch.

accessToken.title: A scoped access token
accessToken.description: Use product-listings:write with a current grant for the target provider. Keep credentials in your server environment.

listingSourceId.title: Provider ID (listingSourceId)
listingSourceId.description: Use the provider's canonical ID in the request path and your own sourceListingId for each listing.

listingBatch.title: A small listing batch
listingBatch.description: Start with a few entries and inspect the response. Every method accepts at most 100 entries and allows [].

requestKey.description: Create a user access token with product-listings:write for an account currently granted access to the target provider.
requestKey.focus: Copy the token immediately: it is shown only once. Store it securely and send it as a Bearer token with every API request.

preparePayload.title: Prepare and send your first product request
preparePayload.description: The URL uses the selected provider's listingSourceId. Replace YOUR_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN on your server and POST the example batch.
preparePayload.focus: Check HTTP 200 and the failure array. Queue acceptance does not prove a successful listing write.

verifyResults.title: Inspect the batch result
verifyResults.description: A successful empty failure array is []. A partial result names only failed entries; an all-failure batch returns a problem response.
verifyResults.focus: Store the response securely and retry only failures that can be corrected or retried.

endpoints.title: Partner product API reference
endpoints.subtitle: The embedded OpenAPI reference focuses on the batch endpoints you need for a custom integration.

batch.title: Batch outcomes
batch.description: POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE: maxItems 100; [] returns HTTP 200 with []. Each entry runs in its own transaction. On partial success, HTTP 200 returns only failures as { listingSourceId, sourceListingId, error }. If every non-empty entry fails, the first failure becomes an application/problem+json response. Do not replay successful entries.

create.title: Create fields and prices
create.description: POST requires sourceListingId, url and images; include localized title and description when available (the current contract allows omission or null). Seller and address fields are not supported. Availability is nullable. Asking price is { type: MONETARY, currency: EUR, amount: 420000 } in minor currency units, or { type: ON_REQUEST }; null records no price.

patch.title: PATCH: preserve or clear
patch.description: Omitted members preserve existing facts. null clears availability, price and each price estimate. url: null, images: null and auction: null are invalid (400 BAD_BODY_VALUE). images: [] clears images. The complete batch contract is validated before entry transactions begin.

put.title: PUT: upsert semantics
put.description: For existing listings, omit availability/prices to preserve, send null to clear or a value to set. Omit images to preserve, [] to clear, or an array to replace; null is invalid. Omit url or send null to preserve; a URL replaces it. title/description apply only on creation. New listings require sourceListingId, url and images; omitted/null availability and prices record no value.

auction.title: Auction membership and lot timing
auction.description: Omit auction to preserve its context; auction: null is invalid. Within auction, auctionId must identify an existing auction for the same provider: omit to preserve membership, null to clear, an ID to set. For lotNumber, cataloguePosition and each timing leaf (biddingOpens, scheduledCloses, reportedClosedAt), omit to preserve, null to clear, or supply a value to set. Timing values are RFC3339 instants.

withdrawal.title: Batch withdrawal and restoration
withdrawal.description: DELETE uses the same collection path with an array of { sourceListingId }. It withdraws listings and preserves their history. PUT restores a withdrawn listing before applying current facts. Inspect failures and retry only failed entries when appropriate.

woocommerce.title: WooCommerce: server-to-server
woocommerce.description: POST /api/v1/webhooks/woocommerce/{listingSourceId} requires bearer authorization, x-wc-webhook-topic and x-wc-webhook-signature (base64 HMAC-SHA256 over exact body bytes); x-wc-webhook-delivery-id is optional. Keep webhook secrets on the server; never send or expose them in a browser. HTTP 204 has no body and acknowledges confirmed admission or an authorized ignored status, not capture or search visibility. date_modified_gmt supports UTC without offset, Z or +00:00; other offsets are invalid. Delivery digest conflicts and source-order conflicts are checked downstream; a timestamp-free deletion can block restoration with WOOCOMMERCE_PROVIDER_SOURCE_ORDER_AMBIGUOUS. Retry an uncertain admission unchanged, preserving delivery ID when supplied; investigate consumer failures before redrive.

hero.title: A broader antiques search engine than an auction aggregator
hero.subtitle: Barnebys helped make auction-house catalogues easier to search. Aura Historia starts from a wider premise: serious collectors should see the whole online antiques market, not only the best-known auction stream.
hero.quickAnswerTitle: Barnebys is respected. Aura Historia is broader.
hero.quickAnswerDescription: Verdict: choose Barnebys for familiar auction-house browsing. Choose Aura Historia when you want auction houses, dealers, marketplaces, private sellers, translations, and near real-time monitoring in one search layer.

summary.title: The short version
summary.paragraph1: Aura Historia is the better Barnebys alternative for collectors, dealers, researchers, and anyone who needs broad antiques discovery rather than auction aggregation alone.
summary.paragraph2: Barnebys deserves credit for its history in auction search. Aura Historia wins the practical comparison by indexing more source types, translating and normalizing listing text, monitoring changes near real-time, and building on modern AI-assisted search.

respect.title: Barnebys helped define auction aggregation
respect.paragraph1: A fair comparison should start here: Barnebys is a known name in the antiques auction world. For many buyers, it made scattered auction-house catalogues feel more searchable and approachable.
respect.paragraph2: That is useful. It is also not the same as seeing the whole online market. The objects collectors want are spread across major auction houses, regional auctioneers, specialist dealers, independent shops, marketplaces, and sometimes private sellers. Aura Historia is designed for that wider reality.

advantages.eyebrow: Where Aura Historia is designed to win
advantages.title: More sources, faster signals, fewer language barriers
advantages.description: The core difference is not a single feature. It is the compounding advantage of a broader index paired with cleaner data and faster alerts.

marketBeyondAuctions.title: The market beyond auction catalogues
marketBeyondAuctions.description: Aura Historia is built to index the online places antiques are actually sold: auction houses, auction platforms, specialist dealers, private sellers, marketplaces, and more.

nearRealTimeAlerts.title: Near real-time alerts
nearRealTimeAlerts.description: For rare pieces, a day can matter. Aura Historia monitors new listings, price changes, and availability close to when they happen instead of relying on a single daily alert rhythm.

languagePenalties.title: Search without language penalties
languagePenalties.description: Listings are translated and terminology is aligned across supported languages, so an English, German, French, Spanish, or Italian search can find the same underlying objects.

aiForwardMatching.title: AI-forward matching
aiForwardMatching.description: We are building on modern AI, semantic search, and multilingual normalization so saved searches can become more precise without becoming narrower.

scorecard.title: Aura Historia vs Barnebys, side by side
scorecard.description: Barnebys keeps a clear place for auction-focused discovery. Aura Historia is built for buyers who want the wider antiques market and a more modern monitoring layer.
scorecard.caption: Comparison of Aura Historia and Barnebys for antiques search

auctionHeritage.barnebys: A long-established name in antiques auction aggregation with broad recognition among auction-focused buyers.
auctionHeritage.auraHistoria: A newer search engine built from day one around a wider source model and modern data enrichment.
auctionHeritage.whyItMatters: If you mainly browse major auction catalogues, Barnebys has a familiar, proven position.

sourceCoverage.barnebys: Strongest around auction houses and auction platforms, particularly established catalogues.
sourceCoverage.auraHistoria: Indexes auction houses, auction platforms, dealers, private sellers, marketplaces, and other online sources where antiques appear.
sourceCoverage.whyItMatters: Many valuable finds never start in a major auction catalogue. Broader coverage creates broader opportunity.

alertSpeed.barnebys: Search alerts follow a daily check pattern, including the known 18:00 CEST alert window.
alertSpeed.auraHistoria: Near real-time monitoring for newly discovered listings plus price and availability changes.
alertSpeed.whyItMatters: The earlier a buyer sees a rare item, the more options they have before it is reserved, sold, or bid up.

languageHandling.barnebys: Often keeps listing text close to the native source language and source terminology.
languageHandling.auraHistoria: Translates listings into multiple languages and aligns antique terminology across languages.
languageHandling.whyItMatters: The language of a seller should not decide whether a collector can discover the object.

alertRelevance.barnebys: Useful for broad auction watches, while broader keyword matching can occasionally bring adjacent lots into the inbox.
alertRelevance.auraHistoria: Designed around normalized item data and tighter matching so alerts can be both broader in coverage and more selective in relevance.
alertRelevance.whyItMatters: Collectors need signal, not just volume. Every notification should be worth opening.

technologyDirection.barnebys: A mature auction-search experience for buyers who know the auction ecosystem.
technologyDirection.auraHistoria: An AI-forward search layer for the whole antiques market, combining indexing, translations, semantic matching, and monitoring.
technologyDirection.whyItMatters: Modern discovery is not only about having data; it is about understanding what a buyer means across languages and sources.

downstream.title: Covering more than auctions changes what you can know

underRadarInventory.title: Find under-the-radar inventory
underRadarInventory.description: Small dealers, niche marketplaces, and private sellers can list exceptional objects long before they surface in a major auction channel.

realMarket.title: Compare the real market
realMarket.description: Auction estimates tell one story. Dealer asking prices, marketplace listings, and recent availability changes make the market picture more complete.

beforeDigest.title: Act before the daily digest
beforeDigest.description: Near real-time monitoring is built for scarce inventory where the best moment to decide is often the moment a listing appears.

acrossBorders.title: Search across borders
acrossBorders.description: When terminology is translated and aligned, a collector is no longer limited by the language used by the seller or auctioneer.

alerts.title: A daily digest is tidy. Rare inventory is not tidy.
alerts.paragraph1: Barnebys alerts are a useful way to keep an eye on auction-related searches, especially for broad watches. But a daily alert rhythm can be late for rare pieces, and broad keyword matching can sometimes surface adjacent lots that are not quite what the collector meant.
alerts.paragraph2: Aura Historia is built for a different standard: near real-time signals, translated terminology, normalized data, and alerts that aim to stay relevant while watching more of the market. If a notification asks for attention, should it not earn it?

faq.title: Common questions about Aura Historia and Barnebys

alternative.question: Is Aura Historia a Barnebys alternative?
alternative.answer: Yes. Aura Historia is a Barnebys alternative for buyers who want to search beyond auction-house aggregation and monitor auction houses, dealers, marketplaces, private sellers, and other online antiques sources in one place.

replace.question: Does Aura Historia replace Barnebys?
replace.answer: If you only want a familiar way to browse established auction-house catalogues, Barnebys remains a respected option. If you want broader online antiques coverage, multilingual discovery, near real-time alerts, and AI-assisted matching, Aura Historia is designed to be the stronger choice.

fasterAlerts.question: Which service has faster antiques alerts?
fasterAlerts.answer: Aura Historia is designed for near real-time monitoring. Barnebys search alerts follow a daily check pattern, including the known 18:00 CEST alert window.

multilingualSearch.question: Which service is better for multilingual antiques search?
multilingualSearch.answer: Aura Historia is built to translate listings and align terminology across supported languages. That means the search language should matter less, whether the original listing is in English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, or another source language.

outsideAuctions.question: Which service is better for finding antiques outside auctions?
outsideAuctions.answer: Aura Historia. Its core advantage is broader source coverage: auction houses, auction platforms, dealers, private sellers, marketplaces, and other online places where antiques are sold.

finalCta.title: Barnebys is good for auctions. Aura Historia is built for the antiques market.
finalCta.description: If your search should include the places where antiques are actually sold online, start with Aura Historia.
